Definition: Integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance, public employment programs, labor market information
Comments: No evidence of employment services integration with a central data exchange platform in Sierra Leone.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) confirmed. The cited MoCTI strategy source does not evidence exchange integration of employment services. Fresh searches found a standalone Labour Market Information System (LMIS Tracker) run by the Ministry of Employment, Labour and Social Security, and NCRA statements (Biometric Update, Apr 2024 and Jun 2025) that the national ID (NIN) is required for employment, but no source confirms technical data-exchange integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance or labour market data. A 2025 World Bank procurement notice also confirms the government-wide data exchange layer itself remains at prototype stage. Score retained at 0.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone operates a standalone Labour Market Information System (the LMIS Tracker, run by the Ministry of Employment, Labour and Social Security) and the national identification number (NIN) is stated by NCRA officials to be a requirement for employment in the public and private sectors. There is no evidence that job seeker registries, unemployment insurance or labour market information are technically integrated into a government-wide data exchange platform; the exchange layer itself, planned as a Government Service Bus, remains at an early prototype stage.

Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: Data Protection Bill was developed with Ministry of Justice input but no court records/case management exchange documented.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 changed to 2 (Planned). The cited MoICE source concerns the separate Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill and does not evidence justice-system data exchange. Fresh searches found the e-Justice Blueprint, launched 24 March 2025 under the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project, and a Judiciary press release (17 May 2025) confirming a Canadian consulting team was conducting a needs assessment for court digitisation. No evidence yet exists of operational integration of court records or case management with a data exchange platform, so scored as Planned rather than higher.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone launched an e-Justice Blueprint in March 2025 under the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project, setting out a framework to digitise case management, court processes and legal documentation. As of May 2025 a Canadian consulting team was conducting a needs assessment with the Judiciary to scope digitisation of case management and court records. This is a planned initiative rather than an operational integration with government's central data exchange; court records and case management data are not currently exchanged with other government systems.

Definition: Integration of driver's license registration and traffic offence data
Comments: National ID strategy mentions digitizing vehicles as assets linked to digital identities as a future goal.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 changed to 4 (Partially integrated). The cited MoCTI strategy source only mentions vehicle digitisation as a future goal, predating confirmed operational integration. The Calabash Newspaper (Oct 2023) reports the Sierra Leone Road Safety Authority (SLRSA) gaining authorised access to the NCRA identity-verification platform for driving licence applications and vehicle registration, with NCRA describing the systems as fully aligned; NCRA's own 2024 ID4Africa country presentation lists 'Drivers Licence' among services linked to its centralised NIN verification system via API/portal. Traffic-offence data integration with the wider exchange is not separately confirmed (a new SLRSA smart payment system for traffic fines, launched 2025, appears to be a standalone digitisation), so scored Partially rather than Fully integrated.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone's National Civil Registration Authority (NCRA) provides a centralised, API/portal-based identity-verification service that driver's licensing draws on. Since October 2023 the Sierra Leone Road Safety Authority has had authorised access to the NCRA identity-verification platform, requiring the national identification number (NIN) for driving licence applications and vehicle registration, with the two systems described as fully aligned. NCRA's 2024 country presentation lists driver's licensing among services linked to the centralised NIN verification system via API or portal. Traffic-offence data is being digitised separately through a new smart payment system for traffic fines, but this has not been confirmed as integrated with the wider data exchange.

Definition: Integration of passport issuance and immigration control data into the exchange platform
Comments: Sierra Leone is still in early stages of DPI.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 changed to 4 (Partially integrated). The cited World Bank blog (Dec 2025) describes Sierra Leone as generally early-stage in DPI but does not itself evidence passport/immigration integration. Fresh sources — an NCRA joint communique (effective 1 June 2022), NCRA's 2024 ID4Africa country presentation, and a June 2025 Biometric Update interview with NCRA — confirm passport, work permit and residence permit applications require and are verified against the centralised NIN system via API/portal. Full modernisation of the immigration/passport system itself (ePassport, biometric capture) is not confirmed as complete, so scored Partially rather than Fully integrated.
revised_comments: Since 1 June 2022, a joint communique between the National Civil Registration Authority, the Immigration Department and the Ministry of Labour and Social Security has made the national identification number (NIN) a mandatory eligibility field for passport applications and work/resident permits. NCRA's 2024 country presentation lists passport and immigration services among those linked to its centralised NIN verification system, accessible by API or portal, and this is reaffirmed in a June 2025 interview describing the bulk of government services as digitised and interoperable with the NIN system. Full technical modernisation of the immigration case-management and passport system itself, including ePassport and biometric capture, is not separately confirmed.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: DIAL workshops over 18 months involved over 220 stakeholders including civil society in shaping digital governance strategies. GSB is designed to include audit trails and monitoring tools. SLDTP project has public website. Data Protection Bill 2025 includes right to access information. No public dashboard for data exchange operations yet. Limited/moderate transparency.

revision_notes: Original score of 2 (Low - Limited Disclosure) confirmed. Both cited sources verified: the AfricLaw article (Feb 2026) and the SLDTP project website. AfricLaw's reference to 18 months of DIAL workshops with 220+ stakeholders is corroborated by DIAL's own project page on Sierra Leone. No public dashboard or data-exchange-specific transparency reporting was found in further searches, supporting continued classification as Low disclosure. The Value Name wording differs cosmetically from the metadata scale label ('Low - Limited Disclosure' vs 'Low = Limited Disclosure') but the code is correct and unchanged.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone's digital governance reforms have involved substantial multi-stakeholder consultation: an 18-month Digital Impact Alliance engagement brought together over 220 stakeholders, including civil society, in shaping the country's Digital Economy Programme and National Data Strategy, and a further national validation of the Data Governance Strategy in August 2025 drew over 130 participants including civil society and academia. The planned Government Service Bus is designed to include audit trails and monitoring tools, and the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project maintains a public project website. The Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill, validated in November 2025, would create a statutory right to access information. However, there is no public dashboard or published annual reporting specifically on data exchange operations or data-sharing agreements, so disclosure remains limited rather than comprehensive.
